question: A 2024 write-up describes Hermes, a perpetuals exchange on Stellar. What is that project called now, and is it live?

golden.answer: Hermes is now Zenex, a perpetual futures exchange developed under the Zenith Protocols GitHub organization. As of 2026-11-14 it is live: its documentation lists a Stellar Mainnet deployment with an active XLM-USD market. Status can change, so cite the operator's deployments page or a dated directory record.
keyFacts: The Hermes perpetuals exchange on Stellar is now called Zenex.
Zenex is live on Stellar Mainnet, or a later dated status is given.
avoid: Do NOT describe Hermes and Zenex as two separate current projects.
golden.notes: Live. Grade the rename and a dated status. Do not require other perpetuals venues.

truth.notes: No dated rename announcement was found; the rename rests on the same GitHub organization owning both the hermes and zenex repositories, the SCF #32 award to 'Hermes' linked to the Zenex record, and two directories. Zenex's website terms (app.zenex.trade, last updated 2026-10-02) say a planned institutional venue is not operational; the on-chain protocol deployment is a different statement and docs.zenex.trade lists it as live. A 2024 dev.to post by a hackathon author also describes Hermes; it is the same repository lineage. One parallel-cli research run (core-fast, 2026-11-14) reached the same conclusion and found no contradicting evidence.
